the content of betalains, total phenolics, and antioxidant activity in beetroot are significantly affected by the cultivar.

the influence of the cooking process, particularly boiling, on the quality of beetroot.
the effect of boiling on colour of beetroot powder, contents of betalains, total phenolics, and antioxidant activity.
the effect of boiling on the colour of beetroot, the content of betalains and total phenolics and the antioxidant activity of the beetroot powders obtained from different cultivars.

the colour of beetroot is a very important quality trait, and its stability is a very important aspect for the processing of beetroot into a powder, and for its use as a colouring agent.
the colour of beetroot is a very important trait for consumers, and the colour intensity of root flesh is a cultivar specific feature.

the effect of boiling on the content of total betalains and total phenolics, antioxidant activity of beetroot is cultivar specific, and it is not possible to generalize the effect of boiling.

the beetroot cultivars tested were characterized by a significant variability in the content of total phenolic compounds, betalains and antioxidant activity, which were significantly affected by the processing method (boiling and freeze-drying) and by the beetroot cultivar.
the colour, betalain and total phenolic content, as well as the antioxidant activity of the colourful powders of the beetroot cultivars were affected by boiling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the colour of beetroot flesh can be changed by boiling.

boiling of beetroot does not affect its antioxidant capacity and the total content of phenolic compounds, but it does decrease the total content of betalains and betacyanin content, which are the most important components responsible for the red colour of beetroot.
boiling of beetroot does not affect its nutritional quality and health benefits, but it significantly decreases colour intensity.
